title: AnyPoC: Universal Proof-of-Concept Test Generation for Scalable LLM-Based Bug Detection
datasets: Primary campaign: about 2,700 candidate reports across 12 mature projects (Chromium, Firefox, LLVM, Hermes, OpenSSL, FFmpeg, Wasmtime, Redis, SQLite, FreeType, QuickJS, Memcached); 121 new bugs, 108 confirmed, 92 fixed, 46 PoCs adopted as regression tests.
Validation experiment: 192 reports across seven systems, 96 true/96 false, balanced between LLM-Reporter and human-originated reports; raw corpus not found in public repo.
task: Given a candidate bug report and target source, analyze/fact-check root cause, trigger, consequence and oracle, generate an executable heterogeneous PoC, then independently rerun/check evidence. Supports rejecting false reports. General software bugs include logic, robustness and security.
input_setting: Report + source code + executable environment. Analyzer extracts trigger conditions, cause, consequence and oracle; generator iterates with execution feedback and project knowledge; independent checker recreates it in a fresh workspace and validates a concrete signal.
author_relationship_evidence: GitHub profile zzjas identifies its owner as Zijie Zhao, first author of AnyPoC. The repository README cites the exact paper title/authors/arXiv ID; author homepage lists the paper.
source_commit_or_archive: Author repository zzjas/anypoc HEAD e91ed3ade5726e1cf6ddcdde7659ff747952eb1f (Apache-2.0; seven commits visible). Current repo contains src/, project setup, CLI, Docker support and skills. It is an evolving post-paper implementation, not a pinned paper replication package.
license: Apache-2.0 for current author GitHub repo; paper CC BY 4.0.
exact_models: Paper validation: AnyPoC with Claude Code + Opus 4.5 and Codex + GPT-5.2-Codex; baselines use same agents/models. Campaign also uses Sonnet 4.5/4.6, Opus 4.5/4.6, GPT-5.3-Codex.
Current public CLI shells out to installed Claude Code or Codex; model versions follow the local agent configuration.
weights_status: No trained weights. Depends on hosted/CLI coding agents; exact paper model snapshots are not bundled.
evaluation_route: Full arXiv v2 paper (9,990 words) read. Public same-author repo README, pyproject, setup and CLI statically inspected; it contains a bug scanner, PoC generation workflow, project configs, Docker/container support and agent skills. Current README advertises 130+ bugs vs 121 in the paper, showing the repo is evolving. No frozen 192-report validation corpus, raw traces/results or paper table runner was found. Paper reports $5.02/report Claude AnyPoC and $2.61/report Codex AnyPoC. No code execution or model calls.
blockers: Current author repo is an evolving implementation (130+ vs paper’s 121 bugs); no paper-version tag or exact implementation snapshot identified.
Paper’s 192-report benchmark and raw per-run traces/results were not found, so Tables IV–VII cannot be independently replayed from the repo.
Paper depends on Claude Code/Codex with Opus/GPT-5 Codex and Docker builds of large systems; exact model versions and high setup costs limit replay.
The campaign uses heterogeneous OSS systems, not standard Defects4J/BugsInPy/SWT instances; outcomes are not directly comparable with those benchmark scores.
The paper states a valid PoC implies a valid report, but failure to generate a PoC does not prove the report false.
concept_fit: Very high for causal trigger-to-test reasoning: analyzer extracts cause, triggering conditions, consequence and oracle; an independent checker avoids self-confirmation. This is not a cause taxonomy, and PoCs may be scripts/commands rather than unit tests.
recommendation: Top-priority related work for report-to-executable-trigger validation and causal test design. Use as workflow/design reference. Exact paper results are conditional because the same-author repo is a later evolving app and the 192-report set/output traces are absent. For bounded evaluation, pair its ideas with SWT-Bench or Defects4J and label the setting difference; do not substitute the current app results for paper reproduction.
supporting_locations: Paper §§I–VII, Tables II–VII; extracted text SHA-256 08b1ffccfb5842eb66c943a90d6f4f08d026262dabe942b47e55fee292af383b.
Author profile/site identify Zijie Zhao; GitHub README cites exact paper. Current README/pyproject/setup/CLI hashes are in public_evidence/source-audit.json.
Current code has project configs and CLI but no frozen validation corpus or reported experiment outputs.
